title: Elders who hide their talent through fear will lose it
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Independence, Missouri, on 8 August 1831. The elders there had helped dedicate the land for Zion and the temple site. With that work done, many were anxious to go home. A later Joseph Smith history says they asked him what they should do. This revelation was his answer.
summary: The revelation tells the elders who are to return that the Lord is pleased they came. But some would not open their mouths and hid their talent for fear of man. If they are not more faithful, even what they have will be taken. The elders are to make or buy a boat and travel quickly toward Saint Louis. From there Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, and Oliver Cowdery go to Cincinnati to preach. The rest go two by two and preach on the way home, not in haste. Edward Partridge is to give them money, to be repaid by those able. Elders still coming to Zion must not bury their talent and must shake off dust only in secret.

contextNote.title: A talent kept quiet
contextNote.text: The elders had finished their work in Zion and asked what to do next. Before giving travel plans, verse 2 names a problem among them. Because of “the fear of man,” some would “not open their mouths” to preach. Verse 3 states the result: if they stay unfaithful, what they have will be taken. Verse 13 repeats the charge for elders still on the road: do not bury your talent. In this passage, the talent is the gift and charge to preach, and hiding it means staying silent.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 60–63 teaches that the Lord stays with those who share the gospel. Verse 2 names “the fear of man” as the reason some kept silent; what does verse 7 promise those who speak?
reviewNote: Read all 17 verses. Official heading gives Independence, 8 August 1831, to elders who asked what to do after the dedications. JSP historical introduction added Ezra Booth’s report that most were anxious to return home. Kirtland stands for the Ohio churches they were returning to. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
